sections.title: باب 3 — متن (156)

paras.text: Translation: O people! Fear your Lord who created you from one soul, that is, first from it made its pair; then from those two spread out men and women in abundance over the face of the earth. And fear Allah through whom you demand rights of one another, and avoid breaking ties of kinship. There is no doubt that Allah is watching you.

Translation: O people! Fear your Lord who created you from one soul, that is, first from it made its pair; then from those two spread out men and women in abundance over the face of the earth. And fear Allah through whom you demand rights of one another, and avoid breaking ties of kinship. There is no doubt that Allah is watching you.

At another place the purpose of making tribes and families has been told to be merely recognition; otherwise in fact all human beings are of one and the same race.

يٰٓاَيُّهَا النَّاسُ اِنَّا خَلَقْنٰكُمْ مِّنْ ذَكَرٍ وَّاُنْثٰى وَجَعَلْنٰكُمْ شُعُوْبًا وَّقَبَآئِلَ لِتَعَارَفُوْا ؕ اِنَّ اَكْرَمَكُمْ عِنْدَ اللّٰهِ اَتْقٰىكُمْ ؕ اِنَّ اللّٰهَ عَلِيْمٌ خَبِيْرٌ (الحجرات: 13)

Translation: O people! We created you from one man and one woman and made your nations and tribes, so that you may recognise one another. Indeed, the most honoured of you in the sight of Allah is the one who is most God-fearing. Indeed, Allah is All-Knowing, All-Aware.

The Noble Prophet ﷺ too said that no Arab has any superiority over a non-Arab, nor any non-Arab over an Arab; you are all the children of Adam (peace be upon him), and Adam (peace be upon him) was created from clay.

2. Unity of thought

Islam has also given the lesson of unity of thought, so that human beings do not become scattered intellectually and remain strung in one and the same thread.

The following verses of the Wise Quran point to the unity of thought.

paras.text: Translation: At first all people had one and the same religion, but they began to differ among themselves; then Allah sent towards them prophets giving glad tidings and warnings, and sent down books with them in truth, so that in the matters in which people differed He might decide between them. Translation: At first all people had one and the same religion, but they began to differ among themselves; then Allah sent towards them prophets giving glad tidings and warnings, and sent down books with them in truth, so that in the matters in which people differed He might decide between them. And the difference in it was made only by those people to whom the Book had been given, even though clear injunctions had come to them; and they made this difference only out of mutual obstinacy. Then in the matter of truth in which they differed, Allah by His grace showed the believers its path, and Allah shows the straight path to whomever He wishes.

اِنَّ الدِّيْنَ عِنْدَ اللّٰهِ الْاِسْلَامُ ۟ وَمَا اخْتَلَفَ الَّذِيْنَ اُوْتُوا الْكِتٰبَ اِلَّا مِنْۢ بَعْدِ مَا جَآءَهُمُ الْعِلْمُ بَغْيًۢا بَيْنَهُمْ ؕ وَمَنْ يَّكْفُرْ بِاٰيٰتِ اللّٰهِ فَاِنَّ اللّٰهَ سَرِيْعُ الْحِسَابِ (آلِ عمران: 19)

Translation: The religion in the sight of Allah is only Islam. And the People of the Book differed from this religion only after knowledge came to them, out of mutual obstinacy; and whoever does not accept the verses of Allah, then Allah is swift in taking account.

3. Enjoining good and forbidding evil

Islam wants the formation of such a society where the forces of good and virtue prevail, and in the same way the forces of evil and shamelessness are uprooted. The blessed saying of the Noble Prophet ﷺ is that the society in which there is no effort for mutually establishing good and eradicating evil, it is ultimately destroyed. The divine saying is:

كُنْتُمْ خَيْرَ اُمَّةٍ اُخْرِجَتْ لِلنَّاسِ تَاْمُرُوْنَ بِالْمَعْرُوْفِ وَتَنْهَوْنَ عَنِ الْمُنْكَرِ وَتُؤْمِنُوْنَ بِاللّٰهِ ؕ وَلَوْ اٰمَنَ اَهْلُ الْكِتٰبِ لَكَانَ خَيْرًا لَّهُمْ ؕ مِنْهُمُ الْمُؤْمِنُوْنَ وَاَكْثَرُهُمُ الْفٰسِقُوْنَ (آلِ عمران: 110)
